row.why: Saying the date 5/10 he used the counting form خمس; Amal recast خمسة عشرة, he repeated it, and at 06:25 she quizzed him on when the ة drops (engine could have lost the ة, so low).

row.medi_said: Because it's mostly like أغلب men most-- no? Uh, أغلب...
row.amal_said: لا، it's not the first time we discussed this. We never say أغلب من.
row.why: He linked أغلب to its noun with من ('most of'); Amal said no, we never say أغلب من - أغلب joins its noun directly like idafa (she ties it to the idafa rule at 30:10).

row.amal_said: نفس never takes ال before it. Al-always after it.
row.why: He put el- on نفس, the first word of an idafa-like pair; Amal named the rule. A2 (first word never takes el-) fits, so not PROPOSE. Low: at 24:30 he started 'نفس ال-- Oh' just before her rule (her 24:23 line is garbled), possibly a self-fix.

row.amal_said: نفس never takes ال before it always after and it's before the noun.
row.why: He put نفس after the noun with el-; Amal said نفس goes first and never takes ال (idafa order, A2) and he fixed it to نفس الأشخاص at 27:03.

row.amal_said: Why do you not like forget bisha for example?
row.why: He used formal قبيحة for 'ugly'; Amal voiced the dialect word bisha (بشعة) as what he should use - soft, she framed it as a question.

row.amal_said: No, that's my first day. I want you to say the beginning of my day.
row.why: For 'the beginning of my day' he used يومي الأول (my first day); Amal said no and he went to أول يومي. Different slip from A18 (el- on اليوم).
row.proposed_rule: أول in front of a noun means 'the beginning of' (أول يومي); after the noun as an adjective it means 'first' (يومي الأول = my first day).

rulings.why: Duplicate of A28 (same sahabik tani, same Amal fix sahabak al-thaniyin). Her 'it takes ak' answers his 'definitive doesn't take L' and is most likely the engine for 'it takes el' (the adjective takes el-); the -ik/-ak point is not clearly what she corrected.

row.amal_said: What is difference? They are different. ... مختلف أو غير. مختلفين.
row.why: Tier 1, not 2: فرق (difference) and مختلف (different) are different lexical items, not two forms of one word; Amal said 'what is difference? they are different' and he said مختلف، مختلفين (sheet: different (from) | mu5talef | مختلف). First used at 59:14.

row.amal_said: جهزت is like prepared... بس عملت أو طبخت would be a better fit for food.
row.why: For cooking a dish he used جهزت; Amal said it gives 'prepared everything' and عملت/طبخت fit food better, then prompted فعملت at 03:27. Low: she also said 'it could be' and he had asked about the meaning.

row.medi_said: اليوم بلبس بلوزة، أو قميص رسمي
row.why: Describing what he has on today he used habitual بلبس; the participle لابس fits (my reading). B15 not taught yet - filed, not counted.
row.english: today I'm wearing a formal shirt

row.medi_said: so ٱغْلَب most people because it's not ٱلنَّاسُ, so it'd be ٱغْلَب النَّاسِ.
row.amal_said: أغلب after it there's ال. Why did you take it out? ... Whatever the word is after most we say ال.
row.why: Engine wrote ٱغْلَب النَّاسِ, but Amal's 'Why did you take it out?' and his 'Because ناس is not definitive' show he said أغلب ناس without el-; she named the rule.
row.proposed_rule: After أغلب / نفس the next noun takes el- (أغلب الناس, نفس الإشي) unless it has a possessive ending (أغلب وقتي).
